points: Iran’s Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said in a statement carried by state media Friday that two oil tankers caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz, a day after Tehran claimed five other tankers had similar fates.
Since the outbreak of the Middle East war on February 28, Tehran has sought to limit traffic through the strategic waterway, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil consumption.
The United States has in response imposed a blockade on Iranian ports and escorted tankers through the strait.

US Central Command said last month that it had helped Gulf countries export 1.5 billion barrels of oil via Hormuz since the summer and has recently said that all mines have been cleared from the waterway.

About 250 port watchmen at the ports of LA/LB are threatening to strike, which could bring operations to a halt at eight terminals in the port complex.

Members of International Longshore and Warehouse Union (ILWU) Local 26 have authorized a strike but agreed with the Pacific Maritime Association (PMA), which represents employers, to extend the deadline.
Watchmen make up only 2% of ILWU workers at the two ports but work at terminals handling roughly 85% of Long Beach’s cargo and 33% of Los Angeles’ cargo.

items.title: CRPF Deaths Fall To Zero In 2026. Why The 'Red Corridor' Plays A Role
points: The Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) has reported zero deaths of its personnel in 2026, for the first time in decades.
Data on CRPF deaths since the mid-1980s shows that 2026 stands out as the only year with no reported casualties.
For much of the last three decades, CRPF losses routinely ranged between 40 and 100 personnel a year.
Left-Wing Extremism, including Naxal and Maoist violence, accounted for 719 CRPF deaths during the period, making it the single largest cause of fatalities.
Armed groups and terrorists were responsible for 682 deaths, while North-East extremist groups accounted for 519.
In 2013, the Ministry of Home Affairs identified 182 districts as affected by Left-Wing Extremism.

items.title: Nithya Raman, first South Asian to lead Los Angeles, was born in Keralam’s Thrissur
points: Nithya Raman, the Indian-American city council member who was elected mayor of California’s Los Angeles on Thursday, has her roots in Keralam.
The 45-year-old defeated incumbent mayor Karen Bass to become the first South Asian to lead America’s second-largest city, which is due to host the Olympics in 2028.
Raman was born on July 28, 1981, in Thrissur to Tamil Brahmin parents.
Her family lived for decades in a lane adjoining the Ramaswamy temple in Thiruvananthapuram’s Kottakkathu neighbourhood.
Raman completed her graduation in social studies at Harvard University in 2003 and earned her master’s in urban planning from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology.
Raman was first elected to the Los Angeles City Council in 2020, and her campaign was backed by the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA).
After her victory, Raman promised to improve neglected city services in Los Angeles and undertake medical and housing efforts for the homeless in the city.

items.title: Hapag-Lloyd Acquires 25% Stake in Maersk’s Maasvlakte II Terminal in Rotterdam

Photo: APM Terminals German container shipping giant Hapag-Lloyd has completed its acquisition of a 25% stake in APM Terminals Maasvlakte II in Rotterdam, strengthening its ties with Maersk at one of Europe’s most advanced container terminals.

Maersk-owned APM Terminals retains a 75% stake and operational control of the facility, which serves as a key European hub for the Gemini Cooperation, the vessel-sharing partnership between Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd launched in February 2025.
The investment also advances Hapag-Lloyd’s broader strategy of expanding its terminal business through Hanseatic Global Terminals, established in 2023.

For Hapag-Lloyd and Maersk, the deal further aligns their terminal interests at a major gateway for the Gemini network, which is designed around a hub-and-spoke operating model intended to improve schedule reliability.
Harold Kunst, managing director of APM Terminals Maasvlakte II, said Hapag-Lloyd’s participation would support the terminal’s expansion while maintaining its focus on serving all customers.
